about: Lookup tables built from the links in graph.json. Node ids as in graph.json. A link is a map, not a source: cite the claim ids.

req:DEV-AIF-01.name: Keep pages indexable and snippet-eligible, the whole technical requirement for AI features

req:DEV-AIF-02.name: Spend no effort on llms.txt, AI text files or AI-specific markup for Google

req:DEV-AIF-03.name: Structure content for readers instead of splitting it into small chunks for AI

req:DEV-AIF-04.name: Do not block the AI agents you want as visitors

req:DEV-AIF-05.name: Set robots.txt policy per AI crawler by its own token, and know that user-triggered fetchers ignore it

req:DEV-AIF-06.name: Try WebMCP to declare the actions a site offers to AI agents

req:DEV-CAN-01.name: Use permanent server-side redirects (301 or 308) for moved URLs, straight to the final URL

req:DEV-CAN-02.name: Serve one host over HTTPS with a valid certificate and redirect every other origin to it

req:DEV-CAN-03.name: Put exactly one absolute rel=canonical in the server-rendered head of every indexable page

req:DEV-CAN-04.name: Point every canonical directly at a final URL that returns 200, is indexable and is linked

req:DEV-CAN-05.name: Make all canonical signals agree: redirects, rel=canonical, internal links, sitemaps and hreflang

req:DEV-CAN-06.name: Do not canonicalise one language version to another; connect them with hreflang

req:DEV-CAN-07.name: Never leave staging, preview or mirror copies of the site publicly crawlable

req:DEV-CAN-08.name: Make pages that share a URL pattern differ in their main content

req:DEV-CAN-09.name: Keep migration redirects in place long term and judge a move in Search Console, not with site: queries

req:DEV-CAN-10.name: Redirect an old URL only to a page with the same intent, and return 404 or 410 when there is none

req:DEV-CAN-11.name: Never route a crawlable URL's redirects through a URL that robots.txt blocks

req:DEV-ERR-01.name: Return 404 or 410 for removed and non-existent URLs

req:DEV-ERR-02.name: Return a real 404 for unknown routes in single-page apps, or use a documented client-side fallback

req:DEV-ERR-03.name: Never serve error states, empty results or failed data loads with a 200 status

req:DEV-ERR-04.name: Keep temporarily out-of-stock product pages live with 200 and their current availability

req:DEV-HTM-01.name: Wrap each page's primary content in one clearly delimited main area

req:DEV-HTM-02.name: Place the words a page should rank for in its main content, not in footers or sidebars

req:DEV-HTM-03.name: Give every indexable page a unique, descriptive title element in the server HTML

req:DEV-HTM-04.name: Use semantic, accessible HTML: real buttons, labelled forms and a logical heading order

req:DEV-HTM-05.name: Write valid HTML and close every element

req:DEV-HTM-06.name: Never hide text from users, such as white-on-white or off-screen keyword blocks

req:DEV-HTM-07.name: Use real heading, title and emphasis elements instead of styling alone

req:DEV-IDX-01.name: Use noindex to keep a page out of Search, and leave that URL crawlable

req:DEV-IDX-02.name: Do not use noindex, nofollow or crawl-delay to save crawl budget

req:DEV-IDX-03.name: Send robots rules for PDFs, images and other non-HTML files in the X-Robots-Tag header

req:DEV-IDX-04.name: Allow full snippets and large previews with max-snippet:-1 and max-image-preview:large

req:DEV-IDX-05.name: Do not add nosnippet or a short max-snippet unless you accept losing snippets and AI feature use

req:DEV-IDX-06.name: Prefer rel attributes on individual links to a page-level nofollow

req:DEV-IDX-07.name: Use data-nosnippet on a span, div or section to keep one detail out of snippets

req:DEV-IDX-08.name: Use unavailable_after on pages with a known end date

req:DEV-IDX-09.name: Leave notranslate and noimageindex out of templates unless translation or image indexing must be prevented

req:DEV-IDX-10.name: Use the Search generative AI setting in Search Console only to take a property out of AI Overviews and AI Mode

req:DEV-IDX-11.name: Use the Google-Extended robots.txt token to control Gemini training and grounding

req:DEV-IDX-12.name: On sites with explicit content, keep it on its own subdomain or domain and label it with rating markup

req:DEV-IDX-13.name: For an urgent removal, use the Removals tool in Search Console and also return 404 or noindex

req:DEV-IMG-01.name: Put every image that should be found in an element with a src attribute

req:DEV-IMG-02.name: Describe every meaningful image in its alt attribute

req:DEV-IMG-03.name: Place images next to text that explains them

req:DEV-IMG-04.name: List important images in an image sitemap

req:DEV-IMG-05.name: Serve modern, compact image formats with a widely supported file in the img src

req:DEV-IMG-06.name: Keep images out of Search with robots.txt or X-Robots-Tag, not with CSS tricks

req:DEV-IMG-07.name: Give every article a large, relevant lead image and declare it in og:image or markup

req:DEV-IMG-08.name: Keep the IPTC and C2PA metadata that marks AI-generated images

req:DEV-INT-01.name: Give every language and country version its own URL

req:DEV-INT-02.name: Do not redirect visitors automatically by IP address or browser language

req:DEV-INT-03.name: Make hreflang complete: a self-reference, return links and fully qualified URLs

req:DEV-INT-04.name: Use valid hreflang codes: an ISO 639-1 language, an optional ISO 15924 script and an optional ISO 3166-1 Alpha-2 region

req:DEV-INT-05.name: Supply hreflang through one method only: HTML head, HTTP Link header or sitemap

req:DEV-INT-06.name: Build language and market selectors as <a href> links to each alternate URL

req:DEV-INT-07.name: Make each page's language unambiguous by translating the template with the main content

req:DEV-INT-08.name: Differentiate same-language country versions beyond boilerplate and mark them with region codes

req:DEV-INT-09.name: Choose ccTLDs, subdomains or subdirectories by business needs, and never URL parameters

req:DEV-INT-10.name: Publish machine-translated language versions only after human review and localisation

req:DEV-INT-11.name: Write pages in the words, spellings and script the audience searches with, and never add synonym or variant lists

req:DEV-INT-12.name: Mark the text direction of right-to-left and mixed-script titles, product names and URLs

req:DEV-MON-01.name: Verify every production host in Search Console before launch

req:DEV-MON-02.name: Render every template in a headless browser before release and check it in URL Inspection right after

req:DEV-MON-03.name: Watch the Page indexing report and treat its not-indexed reasons as a work list

req:DEV-MON-04.name: Monitor Crawl stats and server logs for verified Googlebot traffic

req:DEV-MON-05.name: Run recurring rendering checks: raw versus rendered HTML, placeholders and console errors

req:DEV-MON-06.name: Audit canonical groups with a crawler on a schedule

req:DEV-MON-07.name: Track AI feature visibility in the Generative AI performance report

req:DEV-MON-08.name: Set up the Search Console bulk data export to BigQuery on large sites

req:DEV-MON-09.name: Add the brand's YouTube, Instagram, TikTok and X accounts to Search Console as platform properties

req:DEV-MON-10.name: Plan releases and fixes around Google's processing times, and judge results only after them

req:DEV-MON-11.name: Measure the time from publishing a URL to Googlebot's first crawl of it

req:DEV-PRF-01.name: Keep connect time and time to first byte low and stable under crawler load

req:DEV-PRF-03.name: Load per-session-billed third-party tools only after a user interaction

req:DEV-PRF-04.name: Keep each HTML response well under 2 MB and put the main content and JSON-LD early

req:DEV-REN-01.name: Server-render the main content and everything indexing depends on (SSR, static generation or hybrid)

req:DEV-REN-02.name: Have all indexable content in the DOM after load, without clicks, typing or scrolling

req:DEV-REN-03.name: Lazy-load with native lazy loading or an IntersectionObserver, never with scroll events

req:DEV-REN-04.name: Do not block JavaScript, CSS or API endpoints that pages need for rendering in robots.txt

req:DEV-REN-05.name: Do not add, change or remove robots meta tags with JavaScript

req:DEV-REN-06.name: Make rendering robust: no slow API dependencies and no unresolved placeholders

req:DEV-REN-07.name: Keep prices, offer counts and other commercial data identical in raw and rendered HTML

req:DEV-REN-08.name: Feature-detect permission-based APIs and WebGL, and render the content without them

req:DEV-REN-09.name: Monitor JavaScript console errors and Content Security Policy violations on key templates

req:DEV-REN-10.name: Keep indexable content out of iframes, and check web components in the rendered HTML

req:DEV-SDA-01.name: Write structured data as JSON-LD by default

req:DEV-SDA-02.name: Mark up only content that is visible on the page and relevant to it

req:DEV-SDA-03.name: Choose the specific types Google documents for its features, and skip generic or irrelevant ones

req:DEV-SDA-04.name: Identify entities with unique identifiers: url, @id and stable IDs

req:DEV-SDA-05.name: Write dates in ISO 8601 and give every date-time a UTC offset

req:DEV-SDA-06.name: Emit each structured data entity once per page, and audit CMS plug-ins for duplicates

req:DEV-SDA-07.name: Describe only the page's main product in Product markup, not related-product carousels

req:DEV-SDA-08.name: Mark up merchant listings completely, with validity dates for sale prices

req:DEV-SDA-09.name: Declare return, shipping and loyalty policies once at organisation level

req:DEV-SDA-10.name: Put the same structured data on duplicate URLs as on the canonical

req:DEV-SDA-11.name: Validate markup in the Rich Results Test before it reaches templates, and monitor it after release

req:DEV-SDA-12.name: Wire Google's SHACL validation rules into the build once they are published

req:DEV-SDA-13.name: Add Article markup with headline, images, dates and authors to every article template

req:DEV-SDA-14.name: Do not mark up self-serving review ratings of your own business

req:DEV-SDA-15.name: State the preferred site name with WebSite markup on the home page

req:DEV-SHP-01.name: Use Product markup for rich results and a Merchant Center feed for the Shopping tab, with identical values

req:DEV-SHP-02.name: Let Storebot-Google crawl product, cart and checkout pages, through robots.txt and bot protection

req:DEV-SHP-03.name: Send conversational product data in the Merchant Center feed: Q&A, product details, highlights and related products

req:DEV-SHP-04.name: Treat product Q&A and specification markup in schema.org as an extra on top of the feed

req:DEV-SPM-01.name: Never manipulate browser history so that Back does not return users to where they came from

req:DEV-SPM-02.name: Do not generate large sets of low-value pages from templates, feeds or LLM output

req:DEV-SPM-03.name: Never serve Googlebot different content from users, and do not build doorway pages

req:DEV-SPM-04.name: Keep the CMS and plug-ins patched and watch for injected pages and links

req:DEV-SPM-05.name: Publish AI-generated text, images and markup only after human review, and show only real authors

req:DEV-SRV-01.name: Let verified Google crawlers through firewalls, CDNs and bot protection

req:DEV-SRV-02.name: Never serve bot challenges or error pages to crawlers with a 200 status

req:DEV-SRV-03.name: Answer planned maintenance and short outages with 503, for a day or two at most

req:DEV-SRV-04.name: Keep robots.txt reachable on every host: 200 with rules, or 404 if there are none

req:DEV-SRV-05.name: Rely only on the fields Google supports (user-agent, allow, disallow, sitemap) and keep robots.txt under 500 KiB

req:DEV-SRV-06.name: Do not put Content-Signal or other non-standard lines between user-agent lines

req:DEV-SRV-07.name: Answer crawlers over HTTP/1.1 (HTTP/2 optional); never run a crawlable host on HTTP/3 only

req:DEV-SRV-08.name: Support conditional requests with ETag or Last-Modified and answer 304 when nothing changed

req:DEV-SRV-09.name: Do not answer crawlers with 401, 402 or 403 on pages that should be in Search

req:DEV-SRV-10.name: Give a crawler its own robots.txt group only when needed, and make that group complete

req:DEV-SRV-11.name: Never use robots.txt to hide private paths; protect them with authentication

req:DEV-URL-01.name: Make every navigational link an <a> element whose href holds a real URL

req:DEV-URL-02.name: Do not navigate with onclick handlers, javascript: URLs, routerLink without href or # pseudo-links

req:DEV-URL-03.name: Route single-page apps with the History API and real paths, not # fragments

req:DEV-URL-04.name: Link every indexable page from the normal navigation or a hub page

req:DEV-URL-05.name: Publish XML sitemaps listing only canonical, indexable URLs with accurate lastmod

req:DEV-URL-06.name: Give each page of a paginated series its own URL, its own canonical and an <a href> to the next page

req:DEV-URL-07.name: Back infinite scroll and load-more buttons with paginated URLs

req:DEV-URL-08.name: Keep faceted navigation out of the crawl with robots.txt rules or URL fragments

req:DEV-URL-09.name: If facet URLs must be crawlable, use & separators, a fixed filter order and 404 for empty results

req:DEV-URL-10.name: Group URLs into meaningful section paths and launch new content under sections Google already indexes well

req:DEV-URL-11.name: Compute the expected URL for every request and redirect variants to it

req:DEV-VID-01.name: Embed each video in a video, iframe, embed or object element that loads without user action

req:DEV-VID-02.name: Give each important video its own watch page

req:DEV-VID-03.name: Describe videos with VideoObject markup and mark key moments with Clip or SeekToAction

req:DEV-VID-04.name: List videos in a video sitemap

req:DEV-VID-06.name: Serve videos fast in a common container with standard codecs, and never block the files

fact:F-012.name: A Search Console setting now lets a site leave AI Overviews and AI Mode, and Google says the setting is not used as a ranking or inclusion signal for regular results.

fact:F-017.name: Google treats network timeouts, connection resets and DNS errors like 5xx server errors: crawling slows down at once, and indexed URLs that stay unreachable are removed from the index within days.

fact:F-025.name: noindex costs crawl budget because Google must fetch a page to see the rule, while URLs disallowed in robots.txt are not fetched at all.

myth:M-001.name: SEO is dead: AI search needs GEO, a new discipline.

myth:M-002.name: Cut your content into short, self-contained chunks so Google's AI can use it.

quote:Q-001.name: Don't worry about what to call it. Good SEO is good GEO, AEO.

quote:Q-002.name: Optimizing for people is optimizing for Generative AI Search

angle:A-001.name: Is SEO dead? Google's own answer from Barcelona
